newsitem.title: UK: Float Interest Doubles BioMedica Valuation.
newsitem.headline: Float Interest Doubles BioMedica Valuation.

text.p: Fledgling gene therapy company Oxford BioMedica Plc said on Monday its potential valuation had doubled as a result of strong interest in its plans to float on the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) next month.

In its full flotation prospectus, Oxford BioMedica said it now hoped to raise up to 11 million stg from the sale of a 22 percent stake in the company, giving it a market capitalisation of 56 million stg.
Originally the company, which grew out of work carried out at Oxford University, had set its sights on raising around 5 million pounds, valuing it at around 25 million stg.

Oxford BioMedica said that some 6.2 million stg of the proposed placing and offer had already been underwritten. It said its shares had been priced at 88 pence each. Trading on AIM is due to begin on December 10.
Stockbrokers Teather & Greenwood, which are advising the company, said it had received "an unprecedented level of interest from the general public in addition to institutional interest in the stock."
A number of recent biotech issues have run into difficulties, with analysts saying investors have become wary of riskier ventures in the febrile sector.

Oxford BioMedica, which was set up by the directors of Oxford University's retrovirus molecular biology group Alan and Sue Kingsman, believes it can transform the way gene therapy is used to combat a whole range of illnesses.
It has already targeted cancer, HIV and Parkinson's Disease.

The company is looking at ways of delivering a therapaeutic gene to the healthy cells of individuals infected with the HIV virus which would prevent those cells from being infected, and at a product which would make cancer cells highly visible to the immune system.
